chapter: Musicians of the era: players, drummers, bassists, pianists
title: McKinney's trumpeters: Buddy Lee, John Nesbitt, Doc Cheatham and Rex Stewart
summary: Jackson recalls Hilton Jefferson and the trumpeters of McKinney's band, including Buddy Lee as swing first trumpet, Nesbitt as arranger, and Rex Stewart's false fingering.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Trumpeters I admired: rating the horn players

blocks.x: Oh, yeah, Hilton Jefferson. Of course, I didn't play with Hilton Jefferson until I 'got to Calloway's band, --
-- but I knew him very well, you know. And there was a lot of great trumpet players that I played with that I could tell you --
Yeah, you've got a list there,
-- and to me, the McKinney Cotton-pickers, there was a trumpet player with him that very few people knew about was a very good trumpet player. His name was George Oliver Buddy Lee.

He played first trumpet with McKinney's on usually the swing things. Langston Curl wasn't a trumpet player that had much range, although he was classed a first trumpet player, but he played first trumpet on the melodic things like they used to in those days. You had a first trumpet player that played all the swing stuff, then the other first trumpet player would play the melodic things. That's the way they used to have it in those days in the bands.
And, of course, before Buddy Lee, John Nesbitt. John Nesbitt was a great arranger also in McKinney's band, and Buddy Lee took his place when he left the band.
And, of course, I can go down -- Doc Cheatham. Doc Cheatham was a very great trumpet player.
No question, still with us in 1976.
Uh-huh. I've worked with him, and, of course, I remember Rex Stewart, you know.
I think you told me the story about Rex in McKinney's band.

Oh, man, he was fantastic. He could play so fast and he used to cover up his valves, like I told you, so nobody would know his fingering because he used a lot of false fingering on his real fast things.
